extracted.intended_audience: newsroom editors, journalists, media strategists, and media researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes audience-driven criteria for what makes news valuable and discoverable in digital environments, based on a large international survey; intended to guide newsroom strategy, format choice, and topic selection. Emphasizes platform, format, trust, and coverage gaps that influence audience engagement and avoidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of underserved topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of underserved topics = unmet audience need (page identifies local news, health news, and education news as coverage gaps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize reporting on local issues/hyperlocal, health practical information, education updates, constructive/solutions journalism and underrepresented communities — these areas have high audience value and low supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive framing = audience preference; constructive/solutions journalism is highlighted as something audiences want more of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame stories to include solutions and practical information rather than only negative or conflict-driven narratives to better meet audience needs and reduce news avoidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual + short-form
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual + short-form = format-driven newsworthiness; visual/multimedia content outperforms text and short-form video dominates younger demographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize image-led and short-form video formats for discovery and engagement, especially to reach younger audiences; adapt story packaging to video-first consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust signals / trusted brands
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust signals are a critical distinguisher — trusted brands matter more amid misinformation and low overall trust in news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in clear sourcing, verification, transparency, brand-building and other trust cues to increase audience willingness to engage and subscribe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Local depth = high audience value, low supply; local news is consistently identified as underserved across many countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop deeper local reporting and hyperlocal beats where possible; local depth can differentiate and meet clear audience demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform selection and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Platform shifts matter for news reach: Facebook for news has declined while TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and private messaging apps are growing; visual/video-led platforms dominate for younger users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose distribution platforms aligned with target audiences and optimize content formats for those platforms (e.g., short video for TikTok, stories/reels for Instagram, messaging-friendly formats for private apps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for personalization and algorithmic discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalized algorithm feeds drive discovery — algorithmic recommendation is a key channel for finding news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize metadata, headlines, thumbnails, recirculation hooks and engagement signals so content performs in personalized feeds; consider how editorial decisions interact with algorithmic discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Niche topics and community signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Niche topics combined with community signals drive engagement; audiences seek specialized coverage and community-relevant signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target niche subject areas and cultivate community engagement signals (comments, shares, community features) to increase visibility and loyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid negativity overload
rubrics_metrics.description: Negativity overload is a driver of news avoidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance necessary reporting of harms/conflict with practical, solution-oriented, or constructive content to reduce fatigue and avoidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid polarization and repetitive conflict coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Polarization fatigue and repetitive coverage of conflict contribute to audience disengagement and avoidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversify topics, provide context rather than repetitive conflict framing, and avoid stoking polarization as a tactic for engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription and monetization realities
rubrics_metrics.description: Stagnating digital subscriptions and variable trust levels across markets affect business models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that subscriptions are not uniformly growing; focus on building trust and value propositions (e.g., niche/local depth, trust signals) alongside experiments with alternative revenue models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile-first and messaging-centered approaches (Global South)
rubrics_metrics.description: In many Global South markets news consumption is mobile-first and centered on messaging apps; countries such as China and India use distinct platform ecosystems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize content for mobile devices, design for distribution via messaging apps, and adapt strategies to local platform ecosystems rather than assuming the same platforms or formats globally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emerging formats: podcasts and AI chatbots
rubrics_metrics.description: Podcasts reach about 10% (similar to print) and AI chatbots are an emerging category (~9%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider audio and chatbot formats as part of a diversified strategy, but recognize their current limited reach compared with visual/short-form video; monitor growth of chatbots as a discovery/interaction channel.
